document_check.note: The source is Choo IH, Chong A, Chung JY, Ha JM, Choi YY, Kim H. 'A Single Baseline Amyloid Positron Emission Tomography Could Be Sufficient for Predicting Alzheimer's Disease Conversion in Mild Cognitive Impairment', Psychiatry Investig 2022;19(5):394-400, doi 10.30773/pi.2022.0014. Its title matches the summaries.md header for Paper 974. Design: a prospective cohort of 75 people with MCI from the community and a Chosun University Hospital dementia clinic, Gwangju, followed annually. The cited number is present: Table 1 gives GDS 10.1 plus or minus 7.7 in non-converters (N=58) against 9.7 plus or minus 7.3 in converters (N=17), p=0.850, and the Results text names the Geriatric Depression Scale among the variables that did not differ.

cited_result: Baseline Geriatric Depression Scale score compared between later converters to AD (N=17) and non-converters (N=58) in 75 people with MCI followed for a mean of 24 months. GDS was 9.7 plus or minus 7.3 in converters against 10.1 plus or minus 7.7 in non-converters, p=0.850, by unpaired t-test (Table 1, p. 3, journal p. 396; Results text p. 4, journal p. 397).
tool_reason: The cited result asks whether one baseline factor, the GDS score, is associated with a later outcome (conversion from MCI to AD). That is a single prognostic factor, not a multivariable model or an index-test accuracy against a reference standard, so QUIPS fits.

domains.rationale: The source population, setting, recruitment period, eligibility criteria and baseline characteristics are all described. However, the number of people screened, eligible or approached is not reported, so the participation rate is unknown. The sampling method is not stated: there is no mention of consecutive or random sampling. Community and clinic recruits are pooled. Enrolment also required amyloid PET, and people with psychiatric disorders or on psychoactive medication were excluded, which bears directly on the range of depressive symptoms the factor can take.

signalling.question: Adequate participation in the study by eligible persons
signalling.quote: Looked in Methods and Results for the number screened, eligible, approached or declining; none is reported. Only the number enrolled is given: 'Seventy-five individuals with MCI were recruited from the community and from the Dementia Clinic, Chosun University Hospital, Gwangju, South Korea from April 2017 to January 2021.'

signalling.question: Description of the source population or population of interest
signalling.quote: Seventy-five individuals with MCI were recruited from the community and from the Dementia Clinic, Chosun University Hospital, Gwangju, South Korea from April 2017 to January 2021.

signalling.question: Description of the baseline study sample
signalling.quote: Table 1. Demographic and neuropsychological test performance for MCI subjects by conversion status

signalling.question: Adequate description of the sampling frame and recruitment
signalling.quote: recruited from the community and from the Dementia Clinic, Chosun University Hospital (no statement of consecutive or random sampling, or of how community participants were identified)

signalling.question: Adequate description of the period and place of recruitment
signalling.quote: Chosun University Hospital, Gwangju, South Korea from April 2017 to January 2021.

signalling.question: Adequate description of inclusion and exclusion criteria
signalling.quote: The participants received a CDR score of 0.5 and met Petersen's criteria ... The exclusion criteria included any current serious medical, psychiatric, or neurological disorder affecting the patient's cognitive function ... presence of severe behavioral or communication difficulties; or a current use of psychoactive medication. Also: 'we only included participants with MCI and amyloid PET.' (p. 7, journal p. 400)

domains.rationale: All 75 recruited participants are accounted for in the outcome classification: 17 converters and 58 non-converters, and the Table 2 rows sum to 75. Every participant had at least one follow-up (minimum 11.6 months). No losses to follow-up are reported. The paper does not say whether anyone recruited was set aside for lack of a follow-up visit, but nothing in it suggests so. Unequal follow-up length is dealt with under outcome measurement and analysis, not here.

signalling.question: Adequate response rate for study participants (proportion of baseline sample available for analysis)
signalling.quote: Of the 75 MCI participants, 17 (22.7% total, or an annual rate of 11.4%) converted to AD. ... Patients in the two aMCI and naMCI to AD conversion groups were defined as MCI converters (n=17), and the other six groups were categorized as MCI non-converters (n=58).

signalling.question: Description of attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
signalling.quote: No drop-outs from clinical follow-up are reported: 'Seventy-five MCI subjects were examined using annual follow-up diagnosis.'

signalling.question: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided
signalling.quote: Looked in Methods and Results for losses to clinical follow-up or reasons for them; none reported. (Only 63 of 75 had repeat amyloid PET, which does not concern the GDS result.)

signalling.question: Adequate description of participants lost to follow-up
signalling.quote: No participants are reported as lost to clinical follow-up.

signalling.question: No important differences between participants who completed the study and those who did not
signalling.quote: Looked for any comparison of completers and non-completers; none is reported because no non-completers are described.

domains.rationale: The GDS is a standard instrument, but the paper names it only in the Table 1 footnote. The Methods describe the clinical interview, CDR, SNSB II and MMSE, but not the GDS: not its version (15 or 30 items, Korean validation), who administered it, or when. The factor is reported appropriately as a continuous mean and SD. Completeness of GDS data is not reported, and the Table 1 APOE percentages do not fit the group Ns, which suggests unreported missing data for at least one Table 1 variable.

signalling.question: A clear definition or description of the prognostic factor is provided
signalling.quote: GDS, Geriatric Depression Scale (Table 1 footnote; the Methods section on clinical and neuropsychological assessments describes 'A comprehensive neuropsychological assessment was also performed annually using the SNSB II, which covers five cognitive domains' and 'Global cognition was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination' but does not mention the GDS)

signalling.question: Method of prognostic factor measurement is adequately valid and reliable
signalling.quote: GDS, Geriatric Depression Scale (named instrument; no version, validation reference or administration procedure given)

signalling.question: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points are used
signalling.quote: GDS 10.1±7.7 9.7±7.3 0.850 ... Values are presented as mean±SD.

signalling.question: The method and setting of measurement of the prognostic factor is the same for all study participants
signalling.quote: Only a general statement is given: 'All participants were examined by clinical interview, which included an assessment of the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR).' Nothing specific to the GDS administration.

signalling.question: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for the prognostic factor
signalling.quote: Table 1 headers give 'MCI non-converters (N=58)' and 'MCI converters (N=17)' with no count of missing GDS values; the APOE row '37.5' per cent of 58 is not a whole number of participants, so missing data exist for at least one variable but are not reported.

signalling.question: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing prognostic factor data
signalling.quote: No handling of missing data is described anywhere in the Statistical analysis section.

domains.rationale: The outcome is clearly defined: AD by NIA-AA criteria at follow-up, assigned at a consensus conference after annual clinical interviews. The weaknesses are these. Follow-up length varied from 11.6 to 42.0 months, so non-converters were observed for unequal and often short windows, and some may be future converters, which the authors acknowledge. The consensus panel reviewed 'all available information' and is not reported as blind to baseline data. That panel was made up of the study authors.

signalling.question: A clear definition of the outcome is provided
signalling.quote: MCI converters were defined when the follow-up diagnosis was AD following National Institute on Aging–Alzheimer's Association diagnostic criteria. MCI non-converters were defined when the follow-up diagnosis was not AD including reversion to cognitively normal and MCI again.

signalling.question: Method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable
signalling.quote: Clinical diagnoses including CDR scores, were made after reviewing all available information in consensus case conferences (authors of IHC, AC, JYC, JMH, HK).

signalling.question: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants
signalling.quote: All participants were examined annually by a clinical interview. ... The mean follow-up duration was 24 months (standard deviation [SD]=9.3; range, 11.6–42.0). ... we had a relatively short follow-up duration of a mean of 24 months and follow-up times variations between subjects

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education and APOE were measured and were used as covariates, but only in the Cox models for amyloid. The GDS comparison is an unadjusted unpaired t-test, and the design does not address confounding for this factor through matching or stratification. Converters and non-converters differed significantly on sex (29.4% against 56.9% female) and on several cognitive scores. None of this is accounted for in the GDS result, so a crude null could mask or distort an association.

signalling.question: All important confounders are measured
signalling.quote: Table 1 reports 'Age (yr)', 'Sex, female (%)', 'Education (yr)' and 'APOE ε4 allele positive (%)'; no confounders are named for the GDS comparison.

signalling.question: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided
signalling.quote: Cox proportional hazards models that included age, sex, education, and apolipoprotein (APOE) e4 allele as adjustment covariates (defined for the amyloid analysis only)

signalling.question: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable
signalling.quote: Looked for how APOE genotype and the demographic variables were ascertained; no method for APOE genotyping is described.

signalling.question: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants
signalling.quote: No description of how covariates were collected beyond 'Their medical history, including stroke or family history of dementia, was also assessed.'

signalling.question: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data
signalling.quote: No missing-data handling is described; the APOE percentages imply missing values that are not reported.

signalling.question: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design
signalling.quote: No matching or stratification for the GDS comparison; design restrictions relate to eligibility only: 'or a current use of psychoactive medication.'

signalling.question: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis
signalling.quote: Demographic and clinical data from the two groups (converter and non-converter) were compared using an unpaired t-test, while the χ2 test was applied to compare proportions and categorical data. ... MCI converters had significantly lower female frequency than MCI non-converters (29.4% vs. 56.9%, p=0.046).

domains.rationale: The GDS result is a bivariate baseline comparison between groups defined by the outcome. It uses an unpaired t-test that ignores the unequal time at risk (11.6 to 42.0 months), although the same paper uses Cox models for amyloid. Only means, SDs and a p value are reported, with no effect estimate or confidence interval. With 17 converters and no power calculation, the null cannot be read as evidence of no association. There is no sign of selective reporting: GDS appears with all the other baseline variables in Table 1, although no protocol is cited.

signalling.question: Sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analytic strategy
signalling.quote: GDS 10.1±7.7 9.7±7.3 0.850 (means, SDs and p only; no difference estimate or confidence interval)

signalling.question: Strategy for model building is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model
signalling.quote: No model is built for the GDS; it is compared in a univariable test: '*significant at p<0.05 for unpaired T or chi-square tests.'

signalling.question: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study
signalling.quote: Demographic and clinical data from the two groups (converter and non-converter) were compared using an unpaired t-test ... Of the 75 MCI participants, 17 (22.7% total, or an annual rate of 11.4%) converted to AD. The mean follow-up duration was 24 months (standard deviation [SD]=9.3; range, 11.6–42.0).

signalling.question: There is no selective reporting of results
signalling.quote: Table 1 summarizes the demographic information and clinical manifestations for baseline measurements for MCI converter and non-converter groups. MCI converters did not show statistically significant differences in terms of age, education, mean cortical amyloid burden, CDR, Subjective Memory Complaints, Geriatric Depression Scale, and APOE ε4 allele ratios, compared to MCI non-converters.

overall: High risk of bias (QUIPS). Study confounding is high, and four domains are moderate (participation, prognostic factor measurement, outcome measurement, statistical analysis). Either the high domain alone or three or more moderates gives high overall under the QUIPS rule.
overall_rationale: Baseline GDS was not a pre-specified prognostic factor. The study's aim concerns amyloid PET ('The objectives of this study aimed to compare the prognostic ability of baseline and longitudinal changes in amyloid burden in MCI patients', p. 1), and the GDS appears only as a Table 1 baseline descriptor. The null comparison is an unadjusted unpaired t-test between groups defined by the outcome. It ignores unequal follow-up (11.6 to 42.0 months), takes no account of a measured sex imbalance between converters and non-converters, and rests on 17 converters, with no effect estimate or confidence interval. The GDS version and administration are not described, and the completeness of GDS data is not reported. The participation rate and sampling method are not given, and people on psychoactive medication or with serious psychiatric disorders were excluded. Attrition is the only low domain.

applicability.rationale: The sample is Korean MCI (CDR 0.5, Petersen criteria) from one hospital clinic plus the community, all with amyloid PET. People with a current serious psychiatric disorder or on psychoactive medication were excluded, so those with treated or clinically significant depression, the group in which a GDS effect would most plausibly show, are under-represented.
The GDS version (15 or 30 items, Korean adaptation) and its administration are not stated, so it is unclear which instrument the null applies to.
Conversion is to AD dementia by NIA-AA criteria over a mean of 24 months (range 11.6 to 42.0). The horizon is short and unequal, which limits transfer to longer-term prognosis.
